q-57187.name: Question 6
q-57187.worked_solution:
Dividing a whole number by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

First, we write $4$ as an improper fraction:

$$
4=\frac{4}{1}
$$

Next, we note that the reciprocal of $\frac{5}{7}$ is $\frac{7}{5}.$ 

So, we have

$$
4÷\frac{5}{7}=\frac{4}{1}÷\frac{5}{7}=\frac{4}{1}\times \frac{7}{5}.
$$

 

Now, we multiply our fractions. 

$$
\frac{4}{1}\times \frac{7}{5}=\frac{4\times 7}{1\times 5}=\frac{28}{5}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{28}{5}=5\,\text{R}3=5\,\frac{3}{5}
$$

q-211475.problem: Expressed as an mixed number in its lowest terms, $3÷\frac{6}{7}=${{field-1}}.
q-211475.worked_solution:
Dividing a whole number by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

First, we write $3$ as an improper fraction:

$$
3=\frac{3}{1}
$$

Next, we note that the reciprocal of $\frac{6}{7}$ is $\frac{7}{6}.$ 

So, we have

$$
3÷\frac{6}{7}=\frac{3}{1}÷\frac{6}{7}=\frac{3}{1}\times \frac{7}{6}.
$$

 

Now, we multiply our fractions. Note that we can simplify the process by swapping the denominators first.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{1}\times \frac{7}{6} & =\frac{3}{6}\times \frac{7}{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\times 7 \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we convert our result to a mixed number:

$$
\frac{7}{2}=3\,\text{R}\,1=3\,\frac{1}{2}
$$
